newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National-NZ First super scheme doomed - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: National-NZ First super scheme doomed - Cullen.

text.p: Ambiguities in the National-NZ First coalition deal raise questions about the coalition's longer term plans for state funded superannuation, Labour Party deputy leader Michael Cullen said on Friday.
He said the way the agreement was drafted should send warning signals to anyone who believed in collective responsibility for the welfare and security of older New Zealanders.
Cullen said it also reneged on a key point of NZ First's election campaign, which was to ensure superannuation payments to 67.5 percent of the average ordinary time weekly wage.

The Superannuation Accord provides that payments should be maintained within a band of 65-72.5 percent of that average wage. Over time payment levels had been drifting back to 65 percent, Cullen said, and the coalition agreement was silent on the issue.
He said present superannuitants would have been better off under a deal with Labour. Its plan addressed the issues of payment levels and promised to increase them.
"New Zealand First promoted its plan as a major step towards ensuring the long term viability of state funded superannuation. If fact it was not and could not be anything of the sort," Cullen said.

He said the deal NZ First had reached with National was doomed to failure. The referendum on the issue, to be held in less than a year, would draw a low turnout and the anti-vote would be high, Cullen said.
